text:
maria: Heads-up — seeing sustained host-memory growth on one Dedicated pool after long-context workloads (65k+ tokens). Hosted looks stable, private on-prem climbs then OOMs. same runtime git hash across all three. :thinking:

raj: what do the slab stats look like? is it kv-slot churn or pageframe growth?

maria: kv slot churn + a lot of pinned pages. here's the quick `smem` snapshot from the failing node: 
```
RSS: 325G
KV-resident: ~290G
AnonHugePages: 0
Mapped: 30G
Cached: 12G
```

olga: looked at perf sample yesterday — NVLink-linked hosts show long stall cycles in the memcpy path and a ton of page pin ops. flamegraph: https://internal/prof/trace/kv-nvlink-2134 (summary: memcpy->pinned_page_wait->jemalloc_arena).

raj: hmm kernel selection also flipped to generic memcpy on that kernel build (we saw fallback to non-optimized p2p kernels after 5/12 kernel updates). did you capture runtime logs? there was an INFO: kernel=memcpy_fast->memcpy_generic around the same time.

maria: yes, found that in /var/log/redwood/runtime.log: 
```
[2026-03-05T14:02:10Z] INFO runtime: kernel_select: memcpy_fast not available, falling back to memcpy_generic (cpu_feature=none)
[2026-03-05T14:02:11Z] WARN kvcache: page_pinned_count=241879 dirty_evictions=0
```

derek: on-hosted the kernel provides the optimized path so no pinned-page hang. on-prem has older kernel + restricted VPC MTU settings that force different NIC offloads -> NVLink + PCIe scheduling gets weird. could be a combination: batching heuristic + slow memcpy => stalling KV reuse and causing incremental growth.

maria: suspect batching heuristics amplify it: when batch sizes spike we keep more KV in memory for reuse windows; if memcopy stalls, the allocator holds onto frames. repro patch: run loadtest with high tail-latency: 
```
./tools/loadtest --model redwood-7b --context 65536 --rps 2 --burst 16 --kv-cache=on
```

olga: quick mitigation: reduce max_batch_tokens and set KV_REUSE_WINDOW_MS=50. also try MALLOC_CONF tweak: 
```
export MALLOC_CONF=oversize_threshold:1,background_thread:true,arena:4
systemctl restart redwood-runtime
```

raj: long-term we should: 1) detect kernel fallback early and reroute to compatible model variant, 2) add a soft cap to pinned-page count that forces early eviction of cold KV pages, 3) make batching heuristic aware of memcpy latency (probe path).

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-318 kv-slab-sat-dedicated-2134; assigned to eng-runtime oncall.

maria: thanks. i'll run the mitigation on the failing node and schedule a canary for Dedicated pool tomorrow at 0200 UTC. will also collect msr/kernel-boot logs.

derek: if you can capture a perf script during a repro that shows p2p stalls I can try building a kernel shim with the optimized memcpy backported.

olga: adding a small perf snippet that exposes the hotspot to the ticket: 
```
sudo perf record -a -g -F 99 -- sleep 60
sudo perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.fold
./flamegraph.pl out.fold > nvlink-flame.svg
```

maria: perfect. thanks everyone. tagging @raj and @derek for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
